svg.aria-label: Fig. M2 Direction predictor, path history, tables and recovery
svg.text: Fig. M2 Direction predictor, path history, tables and recovery
What is measured is the history update rule and the table layout. The provider logic is standard TAGE; the recovery mechanism is the KB conjecture.
on each taken branch (and indirect): shift left by 1 then XOR in the branch bits below
conditional taken: XOR in PC bits 2 to 24 and all 19 offset bits
indirect: XOR in PC bits 2 to 5 and 25 to 30, and target bits 2 to 30
not taken conditional: no shift, no XOR (so a long run of not taken branches leaves the history still)
Consequence: two paths that differ only in a not taken branch share a history; the PC index tells them apart only inside one table block. Measured, single source.
Mapping of which history bit each PC bit lands in is folded and not published; the simulator can carry any
invertible fold. My default: PC bit k lands at history bit (k - 2) mod 32 so one branch touches 23 bits.
Six tagged tables, indexed by PC and history
layout measured; lengths and widths are mine
index = PC[18:2] XOR fold(history, L_i) split by PC bit 6: the two halves of a 128 B block are read together, two branches per lookup (measured)
each table has its own associativity (measured) and 3 bit counters (corroborated); about 44 000 entries in all (derived)
base predictor: not measured. Likely a bimodal table indexed by PC alone, the TAGE default.
Provider: longest history table whose tag matches; altpred: next longest. Allocate on a mispredict into one or two longer tables (cold start writes four, patent).
Training at retire from branch information tables carried from decode, only on mispredicts and weak counters (patent). Loop predictor beside it (patent).
No privilege or process tag on these entries (measured): two processes that collide in index and tag share a counter.
Mispredict penalty 13 cycles (corroborated). 100 branches of history ≈ one history bit per 1.1 taken branches over the window of 144 in flight.
Circular buffer of taken branch footprints
Each branch in flight stores only the head index (7 bits for 144)
instead of a 100 bit copy. On a mispredict the head rewinds to
that mark and the corrected footprint is pushed; the history
register is rebuilt by re folding the footprints after the mark.
Alternative: full copies of both history registers per branch.
No timing probe tells them apart (KB).
Test I would add: a probe that mispredicts once per N taken
branches for N from 1 to 150. Rebuild cost grows with the
number of footprints after the mark under the rewind design
and is flat under the copy design.
Also measured: wrong path indirect branches are squashed as
soon as their target computes, and fetch moves to that target,
so recovery is not serialised on the oldest mispredict.
ITTAGE like, 1024 entries (capacity measured, structure inferred)
tagged tables indexed by PC and the same path history
usefulness bits; a target is kept until it misses twice
entries shared across ASIDs and privilege levels (measured)
a target trained in another context is fetched but not executed (measured)
What the indirect history gets that the conditional one does not
indirect branches fold in target bits 2 to 30 (measured), so the history encodes where the last calls went
so one call site with many targets is told apart by which indirect calls came before it
objc_msgSend method cache: M2 and later only, absent on M1
